stem: Sketch the graph of $y = -4\cos\theta$ for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$ in one smooth stroke, from $\theta = 0^\circ$ to $\theta = 360^\circ$.
solution: Start from the shape of $y = \cos\theta$: it begins at its maximum at $\theta = 0^\circ$, crosses the $\theta$-axis at $90^\circ$, has its minimum at $180^\circ$, crosses again at $270^\circ$ and is back at its maximum at $360^\circ$.
The size of $a$ sets the amplitude. Here $|a| = 4$, so the amplitude is $4$ (an amplitude is a distance, so it is never negative) and the curve reaches $4$ above and $4$ below the midline $y = 0$.
The minus sign in $a = -4$ is not part of the amplitude. It reflects the curve in the $\theta$-axis, so the graph now begins at its minimum, $y = -4$, instead of its maximum.
Join them with one smooth curve. Check: the range is $-4 \le y \le 4$, the period is $360^\circ$, and the curve is the mirror image of $y = 4\cos\theta$ in the $\theta$-axis.
notes:
Genuine fit: the construction is the objective itself (sketch y = a cos θ + q from the effects of a and q), freehand, one stroke, a = -4 and q = 0 inside the cosine limits (|a| <= 4, |q| <= 3) and the curve stays within -4..4. Negative a is deliberate: it is the book's own example of the one misconception this objective lists, and the anchor's 4 cos θ curve (k(x) in the book's figure) reflected. DIAGNOSTIC CAVEAT: curve_sketcher has no reflection predicate for sine/cosine (opens-wrong-way exists only for quadratic). A student who reads the minus sign as part of the amplitude and so draws 4 cos θ, not -4 cos θ, gets the amplitude, the midline and the period right, so none of amplitude-wrong, vertical-shift-wrong or period-wrong can fire for them; what remains is off-target. I map off-target to negative-amplitude because, in this q = 0 template, an unreflected cosine is the dominant way to fail while the three named properties are right. The same predicate would also fire for a sine-shaped or scribbled stroke (a phase error that the instrument does not name); if the scorer reports reflection under another predicate, re-map. The misconception as worded (STATING the amplitude as -4) is an answer-box error; the sketch can only expose its consequence. See the gap recorded for this objective. Other predicates a sketch could fire (amplitude-wrong, period-wrong, partial-coverage, fails-vertical-line-test) are not mapped: this objective's own misconception list holds no error they reveal.

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit): coordinate-notation: the book's (x; y) written (x, y) in solution step 4 (assemble_lesson_bundle.normalise_pairs, the rule every book question goes through; decision 15).
